a:r.a:t: Allosterically activates a variety of enzymes including cAMP-dependent protein kinase A (PKA).
PKA activation leads to activation of enzymes that release glucose from glycogen.

p:cNvPr.descr: Diagram of the transduction of the epinephrine signal using the β-adrenergic pathway; this is part b, a continuation to part a. " Diagram b: From left to right, a -O bonds right to a P, which bonds down to an O-, double bonds up to an O, and bonds right to an O. This O bonds right to P, which double bonds up to an O, bonds down to an O-, and bonds right to O. The O bonds right to P, which double bonds up to O, bonds down to O-, and bonds right to O, which bonds right to CH2. CH2 bonds down to an H on a pentagon with the three bottom lines shaded deeply. To the top right of the H on the pentagon is an O. The point to the right of the O has an H bonded down to it. To the bottom left of that is a point, which bonds up to H on the inside of the pentagon and down to OH. The configuration on the point to the left is the sanme. Above this pentagon structure is a hexagon with alternating double bonds connected to a pentagon with an N at the top, which forms a double bond. To the bottom left of the double bond is a single bond, and on that corner is another N. This N bonds down to the H to the right of the O on the pentagon described at the beginning. The hexagon with alternating double bonds has N's on each of the double bonds, except for the one in the middle that bonds to the pentagon. The top of the hexagon bonds up to NH2. This structure is labeled ATP. Next to it a an arrow pointing right that has a curved arrow coming out of it to the top right pointing to PPi. Underneath the arrows is adenylyl cyclase written in blue. To the right of the arrow is a structure labeled, ""Adenosine 3,5-cyclic monophosphate (cAMP)."" The right side of this structure (hexagon and pentagons) is the same as described before, but the left is different. The H on the bottom left side of the pentagon with thick shaded bottom lines bonds down to an O; this point is labeled 3'. The O bonds left to P, which double bonds left to an O, down to an O-, and up to an O, which bonds right to CH2, with the C labeled 5'. The CH2 bonds down to the H on the left point of the pentagon. To the right is an arrow pointing right that has a curved arrow coming into it labeled H2O. Underneath the arrow is cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase written in blue. To the right of this is another structure labeled, ""Adenosine 5-monophosphate (AMP)." The hexagon and pentagons are the same as previously described, however, the CH2 bonded to the H on the left of the pentagon with the thick lines is bonded to the left to O, which bonds left to P, which bonds down to O-, double bonds up to O, and bonds left to O-.
